claim: A 3-stage curriculum PPO training on Unitree Go1 for reference-free quadrupedal jumping uses 4096 agents and 24 environment steps per update across all stages, with stage-by-stage iteration counts of 3k / 10k / 10k.
stance_target: Curriculum training with multi-billion step budgets is standard for dynamic quadruped skills
scope_conditions: Unitree Go1 quadruped; jumping task; Isaac Gym + RSL-RL PPO; single RTX 3090 GPU
quoted_support: we use 4096 agents and 24 environmental steps per agent per update step. For the vertical jump, we train for 3k iterations, while for the forward jump without and with obstacles we train for 10k steps each.

claim: Wall-clock training time on a single RTX 3090 GPU for the 3-stage quadrupedal jumping curriculum is approximately 10.3 hours total: Stage I ~1.4 h, Stage II ~4.1 h, Stage III ~4.8 h.
stance_target: Single-GPU training of multi-billion-step locomotion curricula is feasible within hours
scope_conditions: Unitree Go1; Isaac Gym; single RTX 3090 GPU; PPO with 4096 environments
quoted_support: Using a single RTX 3090 GPU, the three highly parallelised training stages took approximately 1.4 hours, 4.1 hours and 4.8 hours, respectively.

claim: Each curriculum stage is trained from the checkpoint of the previous stage, with stage transitions being manual (task-level) while within-stage difficulty progression is automatic (success-triggered).
stance_target: Manual task-level + automatic difficulty-level curriculum is effective for acquiring complex legged skills
scope_conditions: 3-stage jumping curriculum; no reference trajectories; PPO; Unitree Go1
quoted_support: The task-level curriculum is, on the other hand, manually selected and consists of training the agent for a certain number of steps at a given task. After mastering the easier jumping skill, the policy is loaded onto the next task.

claim: Reference-free jumping (no motion capture or prior controller imitation) is achievable via curriculum RL alone, achieving 90 cm forward jump on real hardware — claimed to exceed all prior records for similar-size quadrupeds.
stance_target: Curriculum RL without motion references can match or exceed reference-based approaches
scope_conditions: Unitree Go1 quadruped; zero-shot sim-to-real transfer; outdoor grass not seen in training
quoted_support: our policy achieved a 90 cm forward jump on the Unitree Go1 robot, a distance greater than those reported by other model- and learning-based controllers.

claim: Ablation confirms that removing Stage I (jump-in-place pre-curriculum) and attempting to train Stage II directly leads to convergence to a standing behavior, validating the necessity of staged curriculum for sparse-reward jumping.
stance_target: Curriculum staging is necessary (not just beneficial) for reward-sparse dynamic locomotion tasks
scope_conditions: Unitree Go1; forward jumping; PPO; no RSI (Reference State Initialization) vs with RSI
quoted_support: Directly training Stage II without pre-training Stage I, but with RSI height and velocity initialisation... directly training the long-distance jump also results in an early convergence to a standing behaviour, which highlights the need for our curriculum strategy.
numbers: 3k extra steps given to no-curriculum baseline for fairness

claim: Policy architecture is a shared MLP [256, 128, 64] with ELU activations using last 20 observation steps as history; policy frequency 50 Hz, simulation frequency 200 Hz; no separate BC pretraining stage.
stance_target: Network size and architectural choices for PPO jumping curriculum
quoted_support: The actor policy and the critic are parameterised by a shared MLP with 3 hidden layers of dimensions [256, 128, 64]... we found that using the last 20 steps is sufficient for the task while also being fast for training.
